original_question: Does there exist a nonzero real number alpha such that, for every positive integer n, the fractional part of alpha (3/2)^n lies in [0, 1/2)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.2 ("Thue–Siegel–Roth–Schmidt"), unnumbered paragraph after the Waring-problem discussion: the paper defines a Z-number as a nonzero real number α such that the fractional part of α(3/2)^n lies in [0,1/2) for every positive integer n, and states that it is unknown whether such numbers exist. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target very closely: it asks for existence of a nonzero real α, uses the exact multiplier (3/2)^n, quantifies over every positive integer n, and imposes the same fractional-part condition [0,1/2). ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s official terminology is that such an α is a "Z-number." ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))

The paper introduces notation r_n for the fractional part, so the condition is r_n = {α(3/2)^n} with 0 ≤ r_n < 1/2. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
The quantifier is over all positive integers n, i.e. n starts at 1. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))

As stated in the paper, no extra hypothesis is imposed on α beyond α ∈ ℝ and α ≠ 0; in particular, the formulation does not require α to be positive, irrational, algebraic, or transcendental. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
refined_question: Do Z-numbers exist; that is, does there exist a nonzero real number α such that, for every integer n ≥ 1, if {x}=x-⌊x⌋ denotes the fractional part of x, then {α(3/2)^n} ∈ [0,1/2)? ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. Waldschmidt introduces the issue in Section 2.2 while discussing Waring’s problem and the role of estimates involving (3/2)^k, then immediately gives Mahler’s definition of a Z-number and states that it is not known whether Z-numbers exist. So your draft is already aimed at that exact existence problem, not at a broader neighboring question. ([webusers.imj-prg.fr](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/ODP-MoscowMathJ.pdf))
